nodes.label: Signatory Feature Design Document
nodes.rationale: Working document tracking, per topic, the problem, the decision if one was reached, and which answers are still uncertain, so the state of the discussion lives in a file rather than in chat history.

nodes.label: Signatory
nodes.rationale: A person whose name is printed on a document's signature block, not necessarily a system user; under the current design simply an employee chosen for a line, with no separate signatory record.

nodes.label: Signature Block
nodes.rationale: One settled word was chosen for the whole printed block (label, name, printed title) because 'signing line' had been used loosely, sometimes for the block and sometimes only for its label.

nodes.label: Caption
nodes.rationale: A title printed on the paper itself where a person's own title would go. The test is where the words come from, not what they look like: 'GSU Representative' would sit under anybody's name so it is a caption, while 'AO-I/Supply Officer' changes with the person so it is not. The word 'designation' is deliberately avoided because in this project it means an extra role on a group.

nodes.label: Employee History Row
nodes.rationale: One version of a person's name and position title with a date range; a marriage or a promotion each produce a second row so old documents keep the wording they were printed with.

nodes.label: Reference to a History Row
nodes.rationale: A document stores a link to one employee history row rather than the name as text, so a misspelling fixed once corrects every document at once while a genuine name change leaves old documents alone.

nodes.label: Group (TWG, association, BAC Secretariat)
nodes.rationale: A body inside the office that is not a division, section or unit; staff are designated to these on top of their ordinary post.

nodes.label: Per Procurationem (p.p.) Signing
nodes.rationale: Signing on somebody else's behalf with their authority; invisible to the system because it happens with a pen after printing, so the printed name never changes.

nodes.label: Two Rules Per Signature Block
nodes.rationale: Each block carries a rule for who may be chosen and a rule for where the printed title comes from. Both live in the code beside the blocks themselves, because Topic 5 settled that the blocks are fixed and an admin editing them would break the printed page layout.

nodes.label: Who May Be Chosen Rule
nodes.rationale: Three answers observed on real fuel documents: any employee, only staff of a named unit, or nobody at all. The PENR-Officer-only rule was removed on 7 September 2026 because the preparer picks the approver from the ordinary employee list, leaving the General Services Unit as the only restricted case.

nodes.label: Where the Printed Title Comes From
nodes.rationale: Either nothing is printed because the form already carries a caption, or the person's own position title as it stood at the time. There is no third rule for a fixed string; the RIS 'Approved by' only looked fixed because the same person is nearly always chosen.

nodes.label: One Column Per Signature Block
nodes.rationale: Each document gets one column holding a reference to an employee history row or nothing. Because the line is the column name, no 'which line is this' label column is stored, and a blank is legitimate.

nodes.label: employee_history table
nodes.rationale: Built 31 August 2026 with employee_history_pk, employee_fk, the name parts, position_title, valid_from/valid_until and created_by_fk, so every version records who made it. It was the blocking piece because a document stores a reference to a version of a person.

nodes.label: employee_history_correction table
nodes.rationale: A misspelling edits a version in place, which corrects every document at once and would otherwise leave no trace; the log records field, old_value, new_value and who made the repair, which is the accountability the user asked for.

nodes.label: employee table
nodes.rationale: Keeps its current name, position title and short form as the current copy rather than moving them into dated rows, because reading a name is the common case and forcing every screen through a history row would be a great deal of code for no gain. It is written in the same transaction as the current history row so the two cannot drift.

nodes.label: user table
nodes.rationale: Holds login details only and links to exactly one employee; the name fields were moved out so anything showing the signed-in person's name reads through the linked employee.

nodes.label: Short Form Position Title
nodes.rationale: Documents print 'AO-I/Supply Officer' rather than 'Administrative Officer I (Supply Officer)' because the boxes on the paper are small. No rule worth trusting derives one from the other, so somebody types it once. One person has exactly one short form, since varying ones were a typing mistake rather than a real difference, which is why it belongs on the employee rather than per document.

nodes.label: config table
nodes.rationale: A standard one-row-per-setting table with a key fixed in the code and a plain text value the office fills in, chosen so the code can name the General Services Unit without hardcoding a row id that means nothing on another installation. Typed columns were rejected because only one row would ever use them, and a short fixed code column on org_unit was rejected because a field that looks editable while refusing to be edited confuses whoever maintains the office data.

nodes.label: CONFIG_KEYS
nodes.rationale: Holds the key strings the code uses so a typo is a type error rather than a setting that silently reads as empty.

nodes.label: org.gsu_unit setting
nodes.rationale: Renamed from fuel.gsu_org_unit on 7 September 2026 because which unit is the General Services Unit is a fact about the office rather than about fuel; two blocks on two documents read it and a per-report copy could disagree with itself.

nodes.label: fuel.usual_approver setting
nodes.rationale: An optional default added 8 September 2026 after the approver was settled as an ordinary picker. It only decides which name the form starts with, so nothing is restricted and nothing is fixed; leaving it empty legitimately starts both lines blank.

nodes.label: /admin/signatories page
nodes.rationale: A tab per report with one row per setting rather than one row per document, because four rows over two stored values would promise an independence that does not exist; each row instead names the blocks it feeds. Placed here rather than on the Organizational Structure page because it is signatory configuration, not office structure.

nodes.label: admin:view_signatories and admin:manage_signatories
nodes.rationale: Two permissions so a read-only admin still sees the page with the pickers disabled.

nodes.label: org-unit-guard
nodes.rationale: One function answering whether an org unit is named by a setting, called by both the delete and the deactivate paths. A real foreign key would only have protected deletion, while deactivation is an ordinary column change no foreign key can catch, so one mechanism covering both is simpler than two covering one each. The accepted cost is that the protection lives in the program and holds only while every path goes through it.

nodes.label: A Setting Naming Somebody Who Left Reads as Empty
nodes.rationale: The approver setting is checked on every load against active employees and a separated person's id is simply not returned; nothing warns anybody and whoever prepares the next document picks who signs now.

nodes.label: Where a Default Comes From
nodes.rationale: Partly settled. A default never fixes a block, and it has three possible origins: set by an admin (the fuel approver), worked out by the report (the RIS 'Requested by' defaults to whoever is entering the record), or set by whoever handles the report (raised but not yet needed). The rule is that a default is configured here only when nothing else can work it out.

nodes.label: Somebody No Longer Working Is Never Offered and Never Saves
nodes.rationale: Any employment_status other than active counts as not working. Deleting an employee is already refused while anything links to them, so the real case is separation rather than deletion. No warning is raised, because the next preparer simply finds the person gone and picks whoever signs now, which is how the office already works.

nodes.label: The List Is Built From the Document's Filed Date
nodes.rationale: The form asks who was valid on the filed date rather than who is working today, comparing valid_from and valid_until. Reopening an old slip still offers the people valid then, editing needs no special case, and separation must close the current history row or the person keeps appearing on later documents.

nodes.label: Working Group Titles Are Captions
nodes.rationale: Settled by the user with no mechanism needed: such titles are printed on the paper like 'Driver'. Group titles appear on particular documents such as that group's own memoranda, and have never been reused across documents the way a position title is. Designing it earlier was deliberately avoided because no such document had been seen.

nodes.label: Choosing the Wrong Person Is Not the System's Problem
nodes.rationale: The system stops only what is impossible, such as naming somebody who no longer works there. Deciding who ought to sign is the office's job: GSU simply refuses to sign a wrong slip and it is printed again. The control is social rather than technical.

nodes.label: The Separate Signatory Table Is Gone
nodes.rationale: The design until 27 August 2026 assumed a signatory is a person with a typed name and typed position title in a table of its own. Real fuel documents showed nobody's title is ever typed: it is a caption on the form, or fixed, or read from the person's own record. Nothing had to be undone because none of it was built.

nodes.label: Fuel Report
nodes.rationale: Not one form but three documents printed together, which is why Topic 5's one-column-per-block decision now applies per document rather than per report.

nodes.label: Withdrawal Slip
nodes.rationale: Three blocks: 'Requested by' takes any employee under the caption 'Section Incharge', 'Approved by' is GSU personnel only under the caption 'GSU Representative', and the supplier's block is always blank because a gasoline station owner is not in the system.

nodes.label: Driver Trip Ticket
nodes.rationale: 'Approved by' takes any employee and prints their own position title; the certification line takes any employee who can drive and always prints the caption 'Driver', so an ICT Support Staff member can be the driver.

nodes.label: Requisition and Issue Slip (RIS)
nodes.rationale: Four blocks, and the only document whose lines print real position titles. 'Approved by' was first written down as the fixed string 'OIC, PENR Officer' and later corrected: the approver is picked from a list with a usual default, and the printed title is that person's own.

nodes.label: OIC (Officer-in-Charge)
nodes.rationale: The word covers two things and neither needs building. The standing OIC has held the post for years and his own title is what prints; temporary cover while he is away lasts days, never reaches the system, and is handwritten per procurationem.

nodes.label: Signing Happens on Paper Only
nodes.rationale: The system collects no approval and stores no signed-on date; it prepares and prints documents with the correct names. An earlier answer saying signing happened both on paper and in the system created a problem that no longer exists, since signers without an account could never approve and 'not signed yet' could not be told apart from 'will never be signed here'.

nodes.label: A Signature Block May Be Printed Blank
nodes.rationale: Confirmed on paper: the supplier block is always blank and the CDS copy of the RIS has an empty 'Received by' left for somebody to write in by hand, so a report is not incomplete merely because a block has nobody attached.

nodes.label: Topic 1 — A Person's Name Changes
nodes.rationale: Two reasons a name changes need opposite behaviour: a typo was never correct and must be fixed everywhere, while a marriage was correct at the time and old records must be left alone. Storing text on each document freezes both, and nobody would remember which thirty records carried the misspelling. A separate signatory table per report type was rejected once it was clear a spelling fix would have to be repeated in each one.

nodes.label: Two Separate Dialogs for the Two Kinds of Edit
nodes.rationale: Built differently from the topic's original one-Save-button-that-asks idea: 'Add name or position change' and 'Correct this entry' are reached from two different places, so choosing the entry point is what tells the two apart and nobody answers a question after the fact.

nodes.label: add-change-dialog.svelte
nodes.rationale: Ends the current history row and starts a new one, which is the 'record a change that happened' path.

nodes.label: correct-entry-dialog.svelte
nodes.rationale: Edits an existing row in place and carries the warning headed 'This corrects what is already filed', which is the 'fix a mistake in what was typed' path.

nodes.label: Topic 5 — Signature Blocks Are Fixed in the Code
nodes.rationale: Letting an admin add blocks from a screen would let them add blocks to the document, and the blocks sit in fixed positions that must not move, so an editable list would allow the printed layout to be broken. The accepted consequence is that adding or renaming a block is developer work.

nodes.label: Topic 9 — No Conflict Checking Is Being Built
nodes.rationale: Five proposed conflicts were worked through and none produced a check. Three disappeared with the signatory table, choosing somebody who has left became a save rule rather than a warning, and the last was allowed.

nodes.label: The Same Person May Fill Two Blocks
nodes.rationale: Allowed with no warning. The user watched an office head approve their own leave application when the admin officer was away, which is a stronger argument than the project brief's written rule. Nothing about a person makes them ineligible; it is the document that decides whether one name may fill two blocks.

nodes.label: Topic 10 — Record Every Employee, Not Only System Users
nodes.rationale: Full separation was chosen over leaving user untouched (the office's people would then live in two different tables) and over letting user hold rows with no username or password (the login code would be responsible for always excluding them, which is easy to get wrong later).

nodes.label: Not Only HR May Edit Employee History
nodes.rationale: The user's condition for accepting employee history at all. They first rejected it as an HR responsibility EMS should not duplicate, and accepted it only because chosen users can correct a name themselves with every change attributable to a person.

nodes.label: Five Ruled-Out Signature Block Contents
nodes.rationale: The other five reports were closed on 31 August 2026 without holding the paper, by asking whether anything prints inside a block besides a name, a caption, and the person's own title. A group title belongs to the seat so it is a caption; a multi-name block has never been seen, only repeated captions; a non-employee gets a blank line; a PRC licence number is out of scope because such reports are written in a word processor; and a date is always handwritten at the moment of signing.

nodes.label: Appendix — Real Signing Blocks From the Fuel Documents
nodes.rationale: Typed from the physical documents on 26 August 2026 and marked as evidence rather than decision. It is what overturned the guessed design, and it also contains a live example of the typo problem: the same names came out as 'Olaivar'/'Olivar' and 'Gonzaga'/'Gongaza'.
